title: SSRF guard uses allowlist (CGNAT range + ULA IPv6), not blocklist
description: is_valid_fetch_host (peer_fetch.rs) uses an explicit allowlist: for IPv4, only the Tailscale CGNAT range 100.64.0.0/10 is accepted; for IPv6, only ULA (fc00::/7, which contains Tailscale's fd7a:115c:a1e0::/48 range) is accepted. All other IP addresses, including public internet IPs, are rejected. A future contributor might suggest switching to a blocklist (reject RFC-1918, link-local, loopback; allow everything else). That is wrong: it would expose the daemon to SSRF targeting public internet IPs if a malicious peer sends a crafted mailbox_host. The allowlist is correct because Tailscale peers always have addresses in those two ranges.
